findings.summary: TQ-1 (HIGH) is closed: the new RegistratorRegistersThePostSaveTriggerAsAHostedService test genuinely proves the shipped hosted wiring and is non-vacuous.
findings.detail: The test builds a ServiceCollection with host-free boundaries, calls the real ArrTagsServiceRegistrator.RegisterServices, builds the provider, resolves IEnumerable<IHostedService>, and asserts Assert.Single(hosted.OfType<ConfigurationReconciliationTrigger>()) plus Assert.Same against both IConfigurationReconciliationTrigger and ConfigurationReconciliationTrigger. This proves the trigger is registered as a hosted service and that the save path resolves the same singleton that the host starts, so a missing AddHostedService line (which would leave _started==0 and silently no-op RequestReconciliation) fails the test. Non-vacuity is structural: TryAddSingleton<ConfigurationReconciliationTrigger>() and TryAddSingleton<IConfigurationReconciliationTrigger> do not register IHostedService; only the AddHostedService(factory) call does, so OfType would be empty without it. The worker additionally confirmed this by temporarily removing the line (test failed with Assert.Single 'collection was empty').
findings.recommended_action: No change required; the gap is closed.

findings.summary: TQ-2 (MEDIUM) is closed: StopAsyncIsBoundedWhenTheReconciliationIsBlocked deterministically proves the bounded shutdown and cancellation observation.
findings.detail: The test blocks the enumerator (which cancellation cannot interrupt), requests a reconciliation, waits for the scan to enter the blocked enumeration, then asserts StopAsync returns within a 4s bounded wait and under 4s on a Stopwatch while the harness configures a 2s bounded shutdown timeout. After releasing the enumerator it asserts via a bounded stability poll that no hint is enqueued (the loop observes cancellation). The mechanism is sound: StopAsync cancels the CTS and awaits loop.WaitAsync with a linked 2s timeout; ReconcileAsync's cancellation token is cancelled, so once the enumeration returns, ThrowIfCancellationRequested aborts before any enqueue. Ran 12 times with no failure.

findings.summary: TQ-3 is closed: ValidButUnactivatedSaveRequestsNoReconciliation directly covers the valid-but-unactivated case previously verified only by inspection.
findings.detail: SaveHarness(registerSnapshotService: false) leaves the ConfigurationSnapshotService unregistered, so Plugin.TryActivateConfiguration resolves null and returns false. The test asserts the candidate is valid (LastConfigurationValidationResult.IsValid) but the snapshot version is unchanged and trigger.RequestCount is 0. This directly exercises the 'else if (replacementActivated)' branch.

findings.summary: TQ-5/TQ-6 addressed without weakening coverage: vacuous assertions removed and the fixed delay replaced by a bounded stability poll.
findings.detail: The removed Assert.False(release.IsSet)/Assert.Empty(Hints) were vacuous (they hold regardless of implementation because the enumerator is still blocked); the load-bearing assertion (the save task completes within 5s while the scan is blocked, which would deadlock on a synchronous scan) is retained, and the test still awaits the scan-entered signal. The fixed Task.Delay(200) in the coalescing test is replaced by AssertStableAsync, a 300ms bounded poll asserting the enumeration count stays 2; this is deterministic because after the single rerun requestedVersion==servedVersion, so a third run cannot occur.
